DUPLICATE check against the roster's 'Joliet trio' (P0195 Guardian, P0201 Horizon, P0214 Midwestern): independently confirmed distinct -- DT Midstream's own current asset page lists Midwestern's interconnects as including 'Guardian Pipeline' by name (i.e. Guardian and Midwestern are adjacent/interconnecting systems at the Chicago Hub, not the same pipe), and Rigzone's Nov 2024 article explicitly describes them as two separate, 'interconnected' systems within the same 3-pipeline ONEOK->DT Midstream sale. validity.recommendation: update LengthKnown from 366.00 mi to 402.00 mi -- the pipeline has grown since the 2011 vintage of the recorded figure
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's recorded LengthKnown=366.00 mi exactly matches a single-source vintage (Hart Energy, Sept 2011) that was accurate for its time, but is now stale. The CURRENT operator (DT Midstream's own current asset page, dateModified 2026-09-03) states the pipeline is now '402-mile'. This is corroborated directionally by two additional independent sources describing an intermediate 'approximately 400-mile' figure: ONEOK's own 2014 PRNewswire pre-filing announcement, and Rigzone's Nov 2024 third-party trade-press article on the ONEOK->DT Midstream sale ('Midwestern Gas Transmission is a bi-directional interstate pipeline measuring approximately 400 miles'). The growth is consistent with FERC's own 2005 Eastern Extension Project certificate application (Docket CP05-372-000, govinfo E5-3239: 'approximately 30 miles of 16-inch diameter pipeline...in Sumner and Trousdale Counties, Tennessee'), filed after the pre-2011 baseline and before the 400-mile figures start appearing -- i.e. a documented physical-extension project explains most of the growth from a pre-Extension mainline to today's 402 miles.

validity.recommendation: update Capacity from 650.00 MMcf/d to approximately 1500.00 MMcf/d -- current design capacity is more than double the recorded 2011-vintage figure
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's recorded Capacity=650.00 MMcf/d exactly matches the same single-source 2011 vintage as the stale Length figure (Hart Energy: 'a total capacity of 650 million cubic feet per day'). DT Midstream's own current asset page (dateModified 2026-09-03) now states 'approximately 1.5 Bcf/d of design transportation capacity with 82,900 HP of installed compression' -- more than double. This growth direction is corroborated by two documented FERC capacity-expansion filings on this exact pipeline: the 2005 Eastern Extension Project (+120,000 Dth/d, govinfo E5-3239) and the 2023 MGT Southbound Project (+158,000 Dth/d / $6.4 million estimated cost, in Edgar and Vermilion Counties IL and Ohio County KY, to 'allow for bi-directional flow', per the Federal Register notice) -- together these two documented projects account for +278,000 Dth/d (~278 MMcf/d) of the ~850 MMcf/d total increase, meaning further undocumented compression/looping additions (consistent with the stated 82,900 HP of installed compression and the seven-compressor-station baseline noted by Hart Energy in 2011) make up the remainder. The precise current '~1.5 Bcf/d' figure itself is single-sourced to DT Midstream's own current disclosure (kept at medium tier below on the corresponding fills[] entry for that reason), but the magnitude and direction of the change away from 650 is independently corroborated by the two FERC dockets.
